findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the stored-vector validity key incorporates the embedding-model identity AND the pinned digest prompt commit (e.g. fold both into the per-entry freshness key or bump/namespace INDEX_VERSION by model id), so changing either config invalidates and rebuilds the affected vectors rather than cosine-ranking across incompatible embedding spaces.
evidence: Plan: 'both defaults an operator overrides with a model string' — the embedding and digest model are configuration.

ADR 0122 'Freshness key' and src/rebar/similar/catchup.py `_changed`/`dirstate`: validity is the reducer dir hash, which reflects only whether the TICKET changed — an unchanged ticket is 'never re-embedded'.
src/rebar/similar/index.py:39 INDEX_VERSION is 'Bumped when the schema or the indexed text changes' — it is not a function of the configured model.
ABSENCE: the plan nowhere states that a model-string change invalidates or rebuilds stored vectors, nor that the per-entry validity key includes the model id + pinned digest commit.
findings.finding: The vector index's validity key does not incorporate the embedding-model identity or the pinned digest prompt/model, so changing the operator-overridable model string leaves stale vectors (possibly a different dimensionality) in the dir-hash-keyed index and ranks cosine similarity across incompatible embedding spaces.
findings.location: Approach — 'Both model choices are configuration' / 'Ranking swaps behind an interface that already works'
scenarios: Operator overrides the default embedding model to a different provider/dimension; existing per-ticket vectors (old model) are never recomputed because dir hashes are unchanged, and new tickets embed under the new model — cosine similarity is then computed across mismatched vector spaces.
Operator keeps the model but the digest prompt commit moves; digests (hence embeddings) silently diverge from the stored ones with no invalidation.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the predicate that routes a digest reply to retry ('did not answer the task') versus to the empties counter + fallback ('parsed to empty fields'), since both resolve to an all-empty parse in the reference and the plan handles them oppositely.
evidence: Plan 'Two counters' section: distinguishes 'digest parser silently returned empty fields for three reply shapes' from '2 of 630 tickets did not answer the task ... both succeeding on retry'
AC-10: 'A digest reply that does not answer the task is retried'
AC-8/AC-9: empty-field replies are counted and fall back, NOT retried

Reference measure.py has NO retry in `_call_digest`/`build_digests`; both an empty parse and a non-answer currently land in the same all-empty `empties` bucket, so the plan's retry-vs-count split is a new distinction with no stated predicate
findings.finding: The discriminator between the two distinct digest failure states the plan handles differently is never defined. AC-10 retries a reply that 'does not answer the task'; AC-8/AC-9 count-and-fall-back on a reply that 'parses to empty fields'. ADR 0122 records these as separate states (2 tickets 'did not answer' vs. 3 reply shapes that parsed empty), but the plan gives no rule an executor can apply to classify a given reply into retry vs. count-empty.
findings.location: Digest step / Acceptance Criteria AC-8, AC-9, AC-10
scenarios: A reply that is off-task (the ADR's 'began performing the refactoring work') parses to empty fields — is it retried (AC-10) or counted-and-fallen-back (AC-8/9)? The plan's two paths both claim it

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the exact `empties` increment predicate (all four digest fields empty after parse+retry, matching measure.py:599's `not any(...)`), and reconcile AC-9's prose ('an empty field') with its check ('counter equals 3' over the three fully-empty reply shapes).
evidence: Plan AC-9: 'records every digest reply that parses to an empty field ... asserting the counter equals 3'
Reference predicate measure.py:599: `if not any(value.get(field) for field in DIGEST_FIELDS): empties += 1` (all-fields-empty)
digest_document (measure.py:425-432) deliberately yields empty strings/lists for missing fields, so a single empty field is a normal, non-failure state
ADR 0122 Consequences: counter exists so 'a lenient parser without one cannot tell mass failure from success' — i.e. it counts whole-digest failures
findings.finding: The `empties` counter's increment predicate is ambiguous: the plan's AC-9 says the counter 'records every digest reply that parses to an empty field' (singular), but the measured reference increments only when ALL four digest fields are empty (measure.py:599 `if not any(value.get(field) for field in DIGEST_FIELDS)`). Any-one-field-empty would over-count valid digests (e.g. an empty `component_or_area`, which digest_document treats as a legitimately-empty field).
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC-9 ('An `empties` counter records every digest reply that parses to an empty field')
scenarios: A digest whose component_or_area is legitimately empty gets counted as a failure, inflating `empties` and masking mass failure
AC-9's 'counter equals 3' check passes under the all-empty predicate (each of the 3 shapes is fully empty) but the prose implies a different, broader predicate
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite AC-9 to: 'An `empties` counter records every digest reply whose four fields are ALL empty after parsing (the predicate measure.py:599 uses), observable after an index build.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the retry count/bound for a non-answering digest reply (e.g. 'retry once, then degrade to lexical for that ticket') so the behavior is not left to the executor.
evidence: ADR 0122 records '2 of 630 tickets did not answer the task, both succeeding on retry'
AC tests one failure-then-success but does not pin the maximum retry count
findings.finding: The digest retry behavior is specified only by example (AC10: 'fails once then succeeds') with no stated retry count/limit; the number of retries before giving up and degrading to lexical is left to the executor.
findings.location: Approach — 'Two counters ADR 0122 makes mandatory' / AC line 'A digest reply that does not answer the task is retried'
scenarios: A ticket's digest model repeatedly fails to answer the task — unbounded or unspecified retries could stall the build, or a single retry may be intended but unstated
findings.suggested_fix: Specify 'retry once; if the second reply still does not answer, treat the ticket like a provider failure and fall back to lexical for it' to match ADR 0122's observed single-retry recovery.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the scope of the empty-digest fallback: whether a single ticket's empty digest drops only that ticket from vector ranking (build continues, per measure.py) or degrades the whole tier to lexical, and reconcile AC-8 with AC-9's 'build still completes'.
evidence: Plan AC-8: 'When the digest reply parses to empty fields, retrieval falls back to lexical-only with a diagnostic and the create exits 0'
Reference measure.py:678-680: 'one bad ticket must not abort a 630-ticket corpus build, and an empty digest simply retrieves nothing' (per-ticket degrade, not whole-tier fallback)
ADR 0122 Consequences counts empties while 'the build still completes' — per AC-9's own check — implying per-ticket tolerance, not whole-tier fallback
findings.finding: The fallback for an incomplete digest sub-step is under-specified and conflicts with the reference semantics. AC-8 says an empty digest makes 'retrieval fall back to lexical-only' for the whole create, but the reference treats a single empty digest as that one ticket 'retriev[ing] nothing' while the corpus build continues (measure.py:678-680). The plan does not state whether one ticket's empty digest degrades the entire tier to lexical or only drops that ticket from vector ranking.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC-8 ('When the digest reply parses to empty fields, retrieval falls back to lexical-only')
scenarios: One ticket out of hundreds produces an empty digest during a build; AC-8 as worded would drop the entire vector tier to lexical, discarding every other successfully-embedded ticket
AC-8 (whole-tier fallback on empty) and AC-9 ('build still completes' with empties>0) describe contradictory handling of the same event

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State, per fallback arm (missing-dependency, denial, timeout, empty-digest), its disposition with an explicit word (e.g. timeout/throttle = transient/retryable vs missing-dependency = permanent), and state that a retryable primary condition is not permanently masked by the lexical fallback.
evidence: 'retrieval falls back to lexical-only with a diagnostic and the create exits 0' repeated for denial, timeout, missing-dependency and empty-digest arms
The plan distinguishes denial from timeout as separate ACs but assigns both the identical 'fall back to lexical, exit 0' disposition with no retryable/fatal word
failure-disposition-contract: a timeout is transient/retryable; collapsing it to a permanent lexical result masks the recoverable leg
findings.finding: The plan adds four fallback arms (missing optional dependency, provider denial, provider timeout, empty digest -> lexical) plus a retry, but never states each arm's disposition using an explicit retryable/transient-vs-fatal word. A provider timeout or throttle is a RETRYABLE condition; silently degrading it to a lexical-only result for that build converts a transient failure into a permanent downgrade — the 1c0d shape, where a recoverable primary is masked by the fallback's own terminal disposition.
findings.location: Approach / Acceptance Criteria (the denial, timeout, missing-dependency, empty-digest fallback arms)
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Failure-disposition contract' line: missing optional dependency and provider denial are permanent/fatal for this build (lexical is the correct terminal result); a timeout or throttle is transient/retryable and the diagnostic must mark it retryable so the downgrade is not mistaken for a permanent config state.
